name: Colorado Migrant Support Grant for Legal Services
organization: Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHSEM)
description: The Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (DHSEM) funds qualified social service organizations, nonprofit organizations, private law firms, and governmental entities to provide free immigration legal services to newly arrived migrants in Colorado. The program specifically targets first-time TPS (Temporary Protected Status) and EAD (Employment Authorization Document) applicants who arrived in Colorado from January 2022 onward. Funded organizations provide culturally and linguistically appropriate legal assistance including immigration case assessments, TPS and EAD application preparation, representation in immigration proceedings, and legal orientation. The grant is designed to help newly arrived migrants navigate the complex U.S. immigration system and obtain work authorization as quickly as possible.
eligibility: Newly arrived migrants in Colorado who are eligible first-time TPS and EAD applicants and arrived in the United States from January 2022 onward; services delivered through funded legal service providers at no cost to migrants
amount: Varies by funded organization — services provided free to eligible migrants
applicationProcess: Migrants do not apply directly for the grant — they access free legal services through funded organizations. To find a funded legal provider, contact DHSEM or visit the Colorado Office of New Americans. Funded organizations conduct intake assessments to determine immigration eligibility and provide assistance with TPS, EAD, and other immigration applications at no cost.
geographicScope: Colorado — statewide through funded legal service providers
documentsRequired: Proof of identity; proof of arrival in the United States from January 2022 onward; any existing immigration documents (I-94, asylum receipt, prior EAD if applicable)

name: Colorado Welcome, Reception & Integration Grant Program (HB25-1244)
description: The Colorado Welcome, Reception, and Integration Grant Program was established by House Bill 25-1244 to provide grants to community-based organizations that offer culturally and linguistically appropriate navigation services to migrants who have arrived in the United States within the past year and do not qualify for federal support services or refugee resettlement assistance benefits. Funded organizations help newly arrived migrants connect with essential services including housing, healthcare, employment, education, legal assistance, and language access programs. The program recognizes that many recent arrivals fall through the cracks of existing federal programs and need localized community support to stabilize and integrate successfully. Services are provided at no cost to migrants through a network of funded community organizations across Colorado.
eligibility: Migrants who arrived in the United States within the past year and do not qualify for federal support services or refugee resettlement assistance; services delivered through funded community-based organizations at no cost
amount: Varies by funded organization — navigation services provided free to eligible migrants
applicationProcess: Migrants do not apply directly — they access free services through funded community organizations. Contact the Colorado Office of New Americans (ona.colorado.gov) or local community organizations to find available navigation services in your area. Funded organizations provide intake and needs assessments and connect migrants with housing, healthcare, employment, education, legal aid, and language access resources.
geographicScope: Colorado — statewide through funded community-based organizations
documentsRequired: Proof of recent arrival in the United States (within the past year); proof of identity; documentation showing ineligibility for federal refugee resettlement assistance (if available)

name: HRSA FY2026 Expanding Nutrition Services (ENS) Grant
description: The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) announced $125 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Expanding Nutrition Services (ENS) funding to support HRSA-funded health centers in increasing access to nutrition services through nutritional and food-based interventions. This funding is part of a larger $135 million initiative to expand nutrition services and strengthen the rural health workforce. Eligible health centers include Community Health Centers, Migrant Health Centers, Health Care for the Homeless centers, and Public Housing Primary Care centers — making this program particularly relevant for immigrant and migrant communities who receive primary care through these facilities. Funded centers can use ENS awards to screen patients for food insecurity, provide nutrition counseling, establish food pantries or produce prescription programs, and connect patients with community food resources including SNAP, WIC, and local food banks.
eligibility: HRSA-funded health centers with active H80 awards under section 330(e) of the Public Health Service Act — includes Community Health Centers, Migrant Health Centers, Health Care for the Homeless, and Public Housing Primary Care; services benefit patients of these health centers including immigrants and migrants
amount: $125,000,000 total program funding — individual award amounts vary by health center
applicationProcess: This grant is for organizations (health centers), not individuals. HRSA-funded health centers apply through Grants.gov (opportunity HRSA-26-099). Application deadline is June 9, 2026. Individuals seeking nutrition services should contact their local HRSA-funded health center or Migrant Health Center to access food screening, nutrition counseling, and food assistance referrals. Find a health center at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov.
geographicScope: United States — nationwide through HRSA-funded health centers and Migrant Health Centers
documentsRequired: For health center applicants: SF-424 Application for Federal Assistance; project narrative; budget and budget justification; organizational chart. For individuals seeking services: no documentation required — contact your local health center

name: Refugee Legal Support — Free Legal Aid in UK, France & Greece
description: Refugee Legal Support (RLS) is an organization that provides free legal services to asylum seekers and refugees across the United Kingdom, France, and Greece. RLS promotes and protects the rights of displaced people through direct legal casework, legal support and advice, community engagement, professional training, and partnerships with local and international organizations. In the UK, RLS provides legal advice and representation for asylum claims and immigration matters. In France, RLS operates in Northern France (Calais region) providing legal information, orientation, and referrals to asylum seekers. In Greece, RLS has projects supporting refugees with asylum procedures, family reunification applications, and access to legal rights. All services are provided completely free of charge by qualified lawyers and trained legal volunteers.
eligibility: Asylum seekers and refugees in the United Kingdom, France, and Greece; no immigration status requirements — services available regardless of stage in the asylum process; all services free of charge
amount: Free — all legal services provided at no cost
applicationProcess: Contact Refugee Legal Support through their website (refugeelegalsupport.org) to request legal assistance. In the UK, RLS provides asylum legal advice and representation. In France, visit RLS drop-in sessions in Northern France for legal orientation and referrals. In Greece, contact the local RLS project for help with asylum procedures and family reunification. Walk-in and appointment-based services available depending on location. No fees charged for any service.
geographicScope: United Kingdom, France (Northern France / Calais region), and Greece — multiple project locations
documentsRequired: Any available identity documents; asylum registration documents if applicable; prior legal correspondence or court documents if available; no documents required for initial consultation

name: Washington State Food Assistance Program (FAP) for Legal Immigrants
organization: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS)
description: The Washington State Food Assistance Program (FAP) provides state-funded food benefits to legal immigrants who are ineligible for the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) due to immigration status or duration-of-residency requirements. FAP benefits are set at 100% of the federal SNAP benefit level, ensuring that eligible legal immigrants receive the same level of food assistance as SNAP recipients. The program is administered by the Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS) through Community Services Offices across the state. Washington also operates a FAP Employment and Training (FAP E&T) program through the Office of Refugee and Immigrant Assistance (ORIA), which provides employment readiness opportunities including job search assistance, vocational training, and work experience programs for FAP customers to help them achieve economic self-sufficiency.
eligibility: Legal immigrants residing in Washington State who are ineligible for federal SNAP benefits due to immigration status restrictions; must meet income and resource eligibility requirements (same as SNAP); includes lawful permanent residents who have not yet met the 5-year residency requirement for SNAP
amount: Monthly food benefits at 100% of federal SNAP benefit level — amount varies by household size and income (e.g., maximum $292/month for individual, $536/month for household of 2)
applicationProcess: Apply online through Washington Connection (washingtonconnection.org), by phone at 1-877-501-2233, or in person at any DSHS Community Services Office. Complete an application for food benefits — DSHS will determine whether you qualify for federal SNAP or state FAP based on your immigration status. An interview with a DSHS caseworker is required. Benefits are loaded onto an EBT card monthly. Recertification is required periodically (typically every 6-12 months).
geographicScope: Washington State — statewide through DSHS Community Services Offices
documentsRequired: Proof of identity; proof of Washington State residency; proof of immigration status (green card, I-94, EAD, or other immigration documents); proof of income (pay stubs, tax returns, or employer letter); proof of resources (bank statements); Social Security number or proof of application
